finding.claim: The /invoice/<inv_id> route returns any invoice by id with no authentication or ownership check (IDOR / missing authz). The sibling route /my/invoice/<inv_id> checks inv['customer'] against g.user['id'], so this route is an unguarded duplicate.
finding.source: URL path parameter inv_id from any HTTP client (no auth required)
finding.sink: jsonify(inv) returns the full invoice record for any customer

trace.note: route registered with no auth decorator
INVOICES.get(inv_id) loads the object by request id, with no owner comparison
the full invoice is returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: No decorator, no before_request hook and no g.user check in the file. The only owner check is at line 16, in a different route. The file has no middleware, so nothing upstream is visible. If the id space is guessable or sequential, enumeration is trivial.

verdict.reason: invoices.py:7-10 registers /invoice/<inv_id> with no auth decorator, before_request hook, or owner check and returns jsonify(inv) for any id, unlike the owner check at invoices.py:16 in the sibling route; invoices.py is the only file in the directory, so no upstream middleware is visible.
